chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Concerto for Jazz Band and Orchestra
summary: RCA asked Sauter-Finegan to record Liebermann's concerto with Reiner; Sauter's judgement of the piece.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: We're getting ahead of ourselves, but since you mentioned that, there's one question I've got to ask

When you had the band, you did "Concerto for Jazz Band and Orchestra" which Rolf Liebereson did and it reached your band and the Chicago Symphony with Rich Reiner, what did you think of that as a piece of music and how did you get involved in it?
We got involved because RCA thought it would be a good thing for us to do. They asked us to.
All of the reviews--I've never heard it.
Oh really? I'll play it for you.
I'd love to hear it because all the reviews I've ever heard of it, Leonard Feather and people like that, really panned it.

It's a typical twelve tone piece of the period. It uses Kenton as the bass and the strange thing is I went to Germany, (inaudible) in 1957 to take over his band. The piece was written for that band. They did it before I got there. It was a Kenton type band.

None of those things have ever come off. I think it's a piece of craftsmanship, the piece is very good. I don't think of it as an artistic success, and none of those things, to me, ever are. I think they are fatuous, in some cases, and begging the question in others.
In those days, and I'm sure Handy and other people thought the same thing (inaudible). The way to do it is here, we have the tools. It was there to be done.
You had guys like Kenton and Boyd Raeburn who said go ahead and write whatever you want.
I think the pre-tention might have come from that side. I don't think it was on the writer's side so much.
Kenton had a way of being quite pretontious. I liked the man very much.
I think I hung onto that attitude for a long time, much longer than I should have, I suppose. Anyway, it was fun while it lasted.
